Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps (post-demo) - ACME Commerce

Hi Sarah + Tom,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap:
- Demo covered: Redwood hosted + dedicated options, routing/fallback, and cost/perf tradeoffs for peak traffic.
- Key ACME needs called out: P0 latency SLO for checkout flows, clear procurement path, and SOC2 evidence.

Requested items / next steps:
1) Could you share a simple stakeholder map or org chart indicating the economic buyer, procurement contact, legal/security reviewers, and the engineering owner for the checkout scope? (A simple XLS/PDF is perfect.)
2) Who will sign as economic buyer (name/title)?
3) Procurement process & timeline: PO vs contract, typical review windows, and any mandatory vendor requirements (SLAs, insurance).
4) Security checklist owner (SOC2, data retention, encryption), we'll loop in Neha (cc'd) from our security team.
5) Preferred intro chain to procurement/legal/security so we can set up brief alignment calls.

I've attached a one-pager that summarizes our offering and the items we typically surface to procurement/legal. If it helps, we can propose a 30-min meeting next week with procurement + security to walk through controls and the mutual action plan.

Thanks, I'll follow up in 48 hours if I haven't heard back.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
redwood.com
